title: Predictive Guardian Intelligence
objective: Detect disk pressure, runaway growth, and structural anomalies using local evidence without acquiring authority.

stories.title: Pressure state model
stories.outcome: Define GREEN/YELLOW/ORANGE/RED from free space, budgets, growth velocity, reclaimability, and active workload.
acceptance_criteria: Pressure is deterministic from inputs and independently testable.
Pressure does not change authority by itself.

stories.title: Growth velocity and forecast
stories.outcome: Estimate provider/project growth rate and conservative time-to-pressure forecasts.
acceptance_criteria: Sparse/noisy history produces insufficient-data rather than false precision.

stories.title: Behavioral baseline anomaly detection
stories.outcome: Build local baselines and flag statistically/heuristically unusual growth without content inspection.
acceptance_criteria: Anomaly score is explanatory and never directly destructive.

stories.title: Structural anomaly detection
stories.outcome: Detect session explosion, unexpected giant files, orphan growth, and provider layout drift.
stories.risk_reclassification_note: Declared CR2 at planning time; raised to CR4 at commit time (round-1 repair) because the change adds ProviderCapabilityAuthority as the ninth wired constraint in rust/crates/cancellai-safety/src/authority.rs - the CR4-floor safety-kernel path (project/risk_floors.json: 'rust/crates/cancellai-safety/src/*') - and a matching cancellai-guardian bridge that reaches it. The addition is opt-in/additive (a new function, not a change to an existing caller's behavior) but it is still an authority-boundary decision, matching this project's own precedent (E12-S03) for raising a declared level once a change actually lands inside the one mutation/authority-boundary seam rather than merely calling it.
repair_history: Round 1 (project/evidence/E14-VERIFIER-REVIEW.md): the layout-drift recommendation reached no authority consumer at all. Fixed by wiring it into cancellai_safety::effective_authority_for_provider_capability via cancellai_guardian::capability_authority.

Round 2 (project/evidence/E14-VERIFIER-REVIEW-ROUND2.md): that fix was a second, optional function next to the pre-existing public effective_authority, and LayoutDriftFinding's public fields let a caller fabricate a fake 'recognized' result. Per the owner's two-round limit, blocked pending an owner-level ADR rather than a third patch attempt.

ADR-0034 (owner decision): provider_capability_ceiling made a mandatory AuthorityInputs field (effective_authority_for_provider_capability deleted; the one effective_authority enforces it for every caller), and LayoutDriftFinding's fields made private with assess_layout as its only production constructor.

Round 3 (project/evidence/E14-S04-VERIFIER-REVIEW-ROUND3.md), the repository's 3-round ceiling, continued past with owner authorization: ADR-0034's mandatory Option<AuthorityLevel> ceiling field was itself a caller-asserted conclusion disconnected from the facts it summarized - a caller could compute the right ceiling once, then separately construct an AuthorityInputs asserting None while still holding the real finding.

ADR-0035 (owner-authorized 4th-round redesign): removes the ceiling as an independent value entirely. AuthorityInputs::provider_layout now carries the raw known_signatures/observed facts (ProviderLayoutAssessment); base_constraints derives the constraint from those facts itself, the identical comparison assess_layout performs. Moved back to ready_for_review for a fresh review round against this design; see the ADR for the disclosed residual it leaves open.

Round 4 (project/evidence/E14-S04-VERIFIER-REVIEW-ROUND4.md), owner-authorized exceptional round: ADR-0035's raw observation was still carried on a plain, publicly constructible AuthorityInputs - a caller holding a real Observed{Drifted} value could still build a second, sibling AuthorityInputs asserting NotAssessed for the same decision. FAIL; no fifth patch cycle on the same field-level approach authorized. Owner directed a structurally different design.

ADR-0036 (round 5, owner-authorized structurally different design): removes the layout fact from AuthorityInputs entirely rather than reshaping it again. effective_authority is now analysis-only (no layout field to discard). A real observation reaches authority only through the new cancellai_safety::resolve_provider_execution_authority, which requires a real, non-forgeable cancellai_platform::BoundLayoutObservation (built from actual directory I/O, never caller-asserted marker strings) and returns an opaque ProviderExecutionPermit with no public constructor. cancellai_guardian::capability_authority (the former bridge) is removed as orphaned by this change. Two residuals disclosed and left open: known_signatures is still caller-supplied (no trusted manifest source wired yet - would need its own dependency-ring ADR since cancellai-safety may not depend on cancellai-provider-api without one), and no mutation-boundary call site consumes a permit yet. Moved back to ready_for_review for independent review against this design; see the ADR for the full account.

Round 5 independent review (project/evidence/E14-S04-VERIFIER-REVIEW-ROUND5.md, Codex, 2026-09-21): FAIL. The round-4 EffectiveAuthority-to-permit bypass was confirmed closed, but BoundLayoutObservation::observe's public identity_observer parameter let a caller pair real markers from one directory with a fabricated identity (via the legitimately-public SyntheticIdentityObserver) equal to a different, genuinely drifted root's real identity - relocating the same class of caller-supplied-fact defect one level down. Classified as repairable within ADR-0036's design, not requiring a new architecture. Repaired by removing the observer parameter entirely: observe(root) now always reads identity via SystemIdentityObserver internally, from the same call that reads the markers. A compile_fail doctest pins the closure. See project/evidence/E14-S04/EVIDENCE-ROUND5-IDENTITY-BINDING-REPAIR.md and ADR-0036's 'Round 5 self-correction' section. Submitted for a second review pass within the same round.

Round 5 second review pass (project/evidence/E14-S04-VERIFIER-REVIEW-ROUND5-PASS2.md, Codex, 2026-09-21): FAIL. The public observer-injection defect was confirmed closed, but BoundLayoutObservation::observe still read identity (symlink_metadata) and markers (read_dir) as two separate path-based syscalls - a same-user concurrent root swap between them could pair one object's identity with a different, replacement object's markers; a final symlink was also silently followed by read_dir rather than refused. Classified as not self-authorized to patch a third time without a fresh owner decision. Owner consulted and authorized implementing the fix plus one further review round.

TOCTOU repair (owner-authorized): observe() rewritten to bind root exactly once via cancellai_sealedfs::SealedRoot::bind_existing (ADR-0017's handle-relative, O_NOFOLLOW-at-every-component walk), then read both identity (new SealedRoot::metadata, fstat on the held descriptor) and markers (new SealedRoot::list_child_names, fdopendir/readdir on a duplicate of the same descriptor) from that one bound object. A symlinked root is now refused outright. Windows/non-Unix fail closed (Unsupported) for both new methods - a new, disclosed, accepted residual, since nothing consumes this API in production on any platform yet. See project/evidence/E14-S04/EVIDENCE-ROUND5-TOCTOU-REPAIR.md and ADR-0036's 'Round 5, second self-correction' section. Submitted for the one authorized review round.

Round 6 (project/evidence/E14-S04-VERIFIER-REVIEW-ROUND6.md, Codex, 2026-09-21, the one owner-authorized round for the TOCTOU repair): FAIL. TOCTOU root-swap and symlink-following defects confirmed closed and the new unsafe ownership/lifetime reasoning confirmed sound, but list_child_names treated every readdir() null result as end-of-directory, so a real mid-enumeration read failure returned a truncated-but-Ok marker list that could coincidentally match a known signature and silently avoid the SI-004 ceiling. Repaired: list_child_names now clears errno before each readdir() call and checks it after a null result per POSIX's documented contract, returning an error rather than a truncated success; the DT_UNKNOWN fstatat fallback failure is held to the same standard. Deterministic regression test added. See project/evidence/E14-S04/EVIDENCE-ROUND5-READDIR-ERRNO-REPAIR.md and ADR-0036's 'Round 5, third self-correction' section.

Round 7 (project/evidence/E14-S04-VERIFIER-REVIEW-ROUND7.md, Codex, 2026-09-21, the one owner-authorized round for the errno repair): FAIL, test-only. Confirmed the production errno/DT_UNKNOWN repair correct, but found its regression test closed the descriptor before list_child_names ran at all, so it failed at the earlier try_clone step and never exercised readdir's own null/errno handling - the test would pass unchanged even with the fix reverted. Repaired: list_child_names rebuilt on a private list_child_names_with_hook (matching this crate's own establish_with_hook/cancellai-platform::mutation's between_open_and_unlink test-hook precedent), letting a new test close the reading descriptor deterministically between two real readdir calls (500 entries, forcing genuine buffer-refill syscalls) and confirm the failure is now reported. See project/evidence/E14-S04/EVIDENCE-ROUND5-TEST-COVERAGE-REPAIR.md and ADR-0036's 'Round 5, fourth self-correction' section.

Structural signals reference concrete observed evidence.

stories.title: Live provider-layout capability gate at the mutation boundary
stories.outcome: Close E14-S04's SI-004 residual, which four independent review rounds across two designs (ADR-0034, ADR-0035) found unclosable by reshaping AuthorityInputs alone: no data shape stops a caller from constructing a second, separate AuthorityInputs that omits or contradicts a real layout observation it already holds, because nothing binds a caller-supplied value to the facts it claims to summarize. This story moves the binding to where it can actually hold: cancellai-platform gains a real provider-root layout observer capability, and cancellai_safety::mutation_executor::execute/revalidate require and consume a live observation from it immediately before any mutation - mirroring how revalidate already re-checks a SealedPlan's preconditions fail-closed immediately before the point of no return (SI-013) rather than trusting what was true at plan-construction time. A caller can still construct as many unconstrained AuthorityInputs as it likes elsewhere; none of them can authorize a real mutation, because the one function that performs one no longer trusts caller-supplied layout data for that decision.
acceptance_criteria: A destructive mutation whose SealedPlan's authority was computed while a provider layout was recognized, but which has since drifted, is refused at execute()/revalidate() time by a fresh observation obtained then - not merely permitted because the plan's own stale data still says recognized.

No caller can reach a destructive authority level for a real mutation by constructing a separate AuthorityInputs/SealedPlan that omits or contradicts the layout observation cancellai-platform's own observer capability would produce for the same provider root at the same time - the exact counterexample E14-S04 rounds 3 and 4 demonstrated must not reproduce against execute() itself.

If the provider root cannot be observed (no filesystem access, an unprobed provider, an I/O error), the result fails closed to the same ceiling a drifted layout would, never to an unconstrained default.
verification: A plan sealed under a recognized layout, executed after the layout drifts, must be refused at execute() time (live-vs-stale regression).

An adversarial fixture reproducing E14-S04 rounds 3/4's own counterexample construction must fail to reach a destructive authority level against execute() specifically, not only against effective_authority() in isolation.
Observer I/O failure/absence fixtures must fail closed, never silently permissive.
